author: Alex Kienlen
title: Beebe fentanyl dealer gets 27-year federal term after overdose death - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Kienlen ,
6 hours ago
LITTLE ROCK, Ark. – United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas Jonathan D. Ross said a man was sentenced on Wednesday to a 27-year prison term for selling fentanyl that resulted in a death.
Ross said 33-year-old Trent Porter of Beebe was given the sentence after being convicted of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl resulting in death. His co-defendants, 50-year-old Lamont Kirk and 43-year-old Willie Johnson, both of Little Rock, were sentenced in 2025 to 13 and 14 years, respectively, for their roles in the conspiracy.
Searcy fentanyl overdose leads to two distinct paths The person whose death factored into the sentences had taken a single fentanyl pill he bought from Kirk on the day he bought it. He died at Kirk’s residence, officials said.
An investigation by the DEA and Little Rock police determined that Kirk had bought the fentanyl from Johnson two days earlier. Further investigation revealed Johnson had purchased the pills from Porter.
When officers arrested Porter, he had 308 fentanyl pills in a bottle in his pocket, officials said. A search of his home revealed an additional 1,617 fentanyl pills. Porter was on active parole with several prior felony convictions, officials said, leading to his sentencing as a career offender.
Methamphetamine surpasses fentanyl in Arkansas overdose deaths After Porter completes his prison sentence, he is assigned three years of supervised release. The federal system has no parole provisions.
